paragraphs.source_en: I had already discovered no fewer than two truths, but the rice cake was still stuck in my mouth, so I felt not the least bit pleased. My teeth were glued fast by the rice cake, and it hurt as if they were being pulled out. If I did not bite through the rice cake quickly, Osan would come in. The children’s singing seemed to have stopped already; they were sure to come running to the kitchen. In extreme agitation, I tried swinging my tail round and round, but it had no effect whatever. I repeatedly pricked up my ears and laid them back down, but that was useless too. On reflection, my tail and ears had nothing at all to do with the rice cake; realizing that I was merely wagging, pricking, and lowering them in vain, I stopped. At last it occurred to me that I must use my forepaws to brush the rice cake off. First I raised my right paw and rubbed around my mouth. Naturally, a mere rubbing was not going to break the rice cake loose. So then I stretched out my left paw and, with my mouth as the center, traced rapid circles. But such spell-casting motions would not make the monster fall away. Thinking patience was the essential thing, I rubbed with both paws by turns, but my teeth remained embedded in the rice cake. Losing patience, I put both forepaws to work at once. Strange, is it not? At that moment I actually managed to stand on my two hind legs. I felt as though I were no longer quite a cat. Cat or no cat, at such a critical moment who had the leisure to worry about that? I resolved that, come what may, I would get rid of this rice-cake monster. Recklessly and with all my might, I clawed all over my face. Because my two forepaws were moving so violently, I kept losing my balance and nearly falling over. Each time I began to fall, I had to steady myself with my hind legs, and so I could not stay in one place. Thus I hopped all about the kitchen, and even I had to admire how skillfully I managed to remain upright. At that moment a third truth suddenly appeared before me: “When faced with danger, one can do what one ordinarily cannot; this is called heavenly aid.” While I, fortunate recipient of this heavenly aid, was battling desperately with the rice-cake monster, I heard footsteps, as though someone were coming from the inner room. I thought, if I were seen at this crucial moment, it would be disastrous. So I bounded about the kitchen all the more desperately. The footsteps came nearer and nearer. Ah, ah, what a pity; heaven’s aid was not quite enough. At last the children discovered me. “Oh, look, the cat ate rice cake and is dancing!” the children shouted. The first to hear the cry was Osan; throwing aside both shuttlecock and battledore, she cried, “Oh my!” and rushed into the kitchen, while the mistress, dressed in her New Year’s crepe formal wear, said, “What a nasty cat!” Even the master came out of his study and cursed, “You fool!” Only the children kept saying, “How funny! How funny!” Then, as if by prior agreement, they all kept laughing in chorus. I was angry, I was in pain, and I could not stop dancing; I was utterly at a loss.

paragraphs.source_zh: 真理已经发现了两个之多，可年糕仍然粘在嘴巴上，所以一点也不觉得高兴。我的牙齿被年糕死死地粘住，痛得就像要被拔掉似的。如果不早点把年糕咬断，阿三就会进来。孩子们的歌声好像已经停了下来，她们一定会向厨房跑来。我烦躁极了，试着来回摆动尾巴，也毫不奏效。我反复把耳朵竖起来又放下去，还是不顶用。想来，我的尾巴和耳朵与年糕毫不相干，不过是白摇尾巴，白竖耳朵，又白白地放下而已，醒悟这一点，我便停了下来。我好不容易才想到必须借助前腿把年糕拂落下去。我先抬起右腿来拂拭嘴巴的周围。只是拂拭一番，当然不可能把年糕弄断。于是我又伸出左腿，以嘴巴为中心急剧地画圆圈。但这种念咒式的动作，是不会使怪物掉下来的。我想耐心最重要，于是我用两条腿轮流去拂拭，可是牙齿依然嵌在年糕里。我发起急来，把两条前腿一齐用上。你说怪不怪？这时候我居然能用两条后腿站立起来。我感到自己仿佛已不像是猫儿啦。管它是猫不是猫儿呢，到了这种紧要关头，哪里还有心思顾及这个呀。我下定决心，无论如何要把年糕这个怪物弄掉。我不管三七二十一，狠命地在脸上抓来抓去。由于两条前腿要猛烈活动，往往失去重心，几乎跌倒。每次要跌倒时，就得用后腿维持平衡，因而无法站在一个地方。于是我在厨房里到处蹦跳，连自己也不得不佩服那灵巧站立的功夫哪。这时第三条真理蓦地浮现出来：“一旦面临危难，则能为平素所不能为之事，此谓之天佑。”有幸享受这天佑的我，正在和年糕怪物拼命搏斗的时候，传来了脚步声，好像有人从里屋走出来。我想，在这种关键时刻给人看见，那还了得！于是我更死命地在厨房里跳来跳去。脚步声越来越近。啊、啊，真可惜，怨天不够保佑呀。终于让小孩发现了。“唉哟哟，猫吃了年糕在跳舞哪！”孩子们大声喊道。头一个听到叫声的是阿三，她把羽毛毽和木拍一齐扔掉，嚷着：“唉哟，可真是……”便跑进厨房里向穿着新年绉纱礼服的主人妻子说道：“这只讨厌的猫！”连主人也从书斋走出来骂道：“这混账东西！”只有孩子们不断地说：“真有趣！真有趣！”然后，她们就像事先约好了似的一齐“咯咯”地笑个不停。我又生气，又难受，跳舞又停不下来，简直是没辙啦。

paragraphs.source_en: Just as the laughter was about to die down, the five-year-old girl said, “Mama, look at the cat; it really is having a hard time.” Thereupon, with what might be called the force of turning back a collapsing wave, everyone laughed at me all over again. I had seen and heard much of human conduct lacking in sympathy, but never had I felt more resentful than I did then. At last heaven’s aid vanished without a trace; I returned to all fours and made the sorry spectacle of rolling my eyes, overcome with embarrassment. It seems the master, after all, could not bear to watch me die, and ordered Osan, “Take the rice cake off him.” Osan looked at the mistress with an expression that seemed to say, “Wouldn’t it be better to let him dance a little longer?” The mistress also wanted to watch me dance, but she did not wish to see me suffocate, so she said nothing. The master said to Osan again, “If you don’t take it off, he’ll die. Hurry and pull it off!” Osan, like someone awakened halfway through enjoying a feast in a dream, reluctantly seized the rice cake and gave it a violent tug. Though my case was not the same as Mr. Kangetsu’s, at that moment I truly feared she might pull out several of my front teeth. It was not a question of whether it hurt or did not hurt; when she mercilessly yanked at teeth firmly sunk in the rice cake, who could endure it? At this point I personally experienced a fourth truth: “All comfort must be obtained by passing through hardship.” When I opened my eyes wide and looked around, everyone in the household had gone into the inner sitting room.

units.source_en: Just as the laughter was about to die down, the five-year-old girl said, “Mama, look at the cat; it really is having a hard time.”

units.source_en: Though my case was not the same as Mr. Kangetsu’s, at that moment I truly feared she might pull out several of my front teeth.

units.source_en: At this point I personally experienced a fourth truth: “All comfort must be obtained by passing through hardship.”

units.source_en: When I opened my eyes wide and looked around, everyone in the household had gone into the inner sitting room.

paragraphs.source_zh: 笑声刚要停下来，那个五岁的小女孩说了一句：“妈妈，你看那猫，也真够受呀。”于是又以所谓挽狂澜于既倒之势，大家又大笑了我一番。过去有关人类缺乏同情心的行为所见所闻不少，但没有比这次更使我感到怨恨的了。终于，老天的保佑消失得无影无踪了，我恢复了四腿着地，并演出了白眼上翻的丑态，我难为情到了极点。看来，还是主人不忍心看着我死去，他命令阿三说：“给它把年糕拿掉。”阿三看着主人妻子，那眼神仿佛在说：“让它再跳一会不好吗？”主人的妻子虽也想看我跳舞，但她并不想眼看着我憋死，所以默不作声。主人又向阿三说：“不给它拿掉会死的，快些给它摘下来！”阿三仿佛梦中赴宴，刚饱享了一半便被唤醒似的，很不情愿地抓住年糕狠命地往下一揪。我的情况虽与寒月君不同，但当时着实担心她可能把我的几颗门牙给揪断。不是什么痛与不痛的问题，她把我死死嵌进年糕里的牙齿毫不留情地这么一扯，谁受得了呀？至此我又亲自体会出第四个真理：“举凡安乐，皆须通过痛苦而得之。”当我睁大眼睛环视四周时，家里的人都到里边的起居室去了。
